statement:
Find the real numbers \(a, b, c, d\) satisfying the system:
\[\begin{cases} a \cdot b + c + d = 6, \\ b \cdot c + d + a = 2, \\ c \cdot d + a + b = 5, \\ d \cdot a + b + c = 3. \end{cases}\]

Consider an \(8 \times 8\) board with all 64 cells initially white. Determine the minimum number of colors needed to color the cells (each one with only one color) in such a way that if four cells on the board can be covered by an \(L\)-shaped tile as shown in the figure, then the four cells are of different colors.

Note: The \(L\)-shaped tile can be rotated or flipped.
figure_description: An L-shaped tetromino covering 4 cells: one cell on top, and three cells in the row below forming an L-shape (the top cell aligns with the leftmost of the three bottom cells).

statement: Let \(n\) be a positive integer. Determine the maximum number of positive integers less than or equal to \(n^2\) that can be colored red such that if \(a\) and \(b\) are both red with \(a \neq b\), then \(a \cdot b\) is not red.

On a table there are 10,000 matches, two of which are inside a box. Ana and Beto take turns playing. On each turn, a player adds to the box a number of matches equal to a proper divisor of the current number of matches in the box. The game ends when, for the first time, there are more than 2024 matches in the box; the player who made the last move wins. If Ana starts, determine who has a winning strategy.

In triangle \(ABC\), let \(A'\), \(B'\), and \(C'\) be points on sides \(BC\), \(CA\), and \(AB\) respectively, such that
\[\frac{BA'}{A'C} = \frac{CB'}{B'A} = \frac{AC'}{C'B}.\]
The line through \(A'\) parallel to \(B'C'\) intersects line \(AC\) at \(P\) and line \(AB\) at \(Q\). Prove that \(\dfrac{PQ}{B'C'} \geq 2\).

An equilateral triangle with integer side length \(n\) is subdivided into smaller equilateral triangles of side length 1 by drawing lines parallel to its sides. Let \(A\) be the set of all vertices of these smaller triangles. A subtriangle is any equilateral triangle whose three vertices belong to \(A\) and whose three sides lie along lines of the original subdivision. We wish to color all points in \(A\) either red or blue such that no subtriangle has all three vertices the same color. Let \(C(n)\) denote the number of such valid colorings. Calculate \(C(n)\) in terms of \(n\).
figure_description: An equilateral triangle of side length \(n = 4\) subdivided into 16 small equilateral triangles of side 1 by lines parallel to the three sides.
